correctness.rationale: Each of the two rows uses n distinct colours and omits one among n+1, say alpha and beta. The top-edge richness condition is exactly that the lower edge in its column has colour alpha, and conversely, so each row has at most one rich edge. Rich-neighbor requires a different adjacent rich edge for each edge, hence both rows have a rich edge in the SAME unique column. Richness there forces complementary missing colours, leaving a common n-1-colour set. Other columns are exactly two permutations differing at every coordinate, i.e. a derangement. Conversely such a colouring satisfies the condition. Counting column, ordered exceptional colour pair, upper permutation and lower derangement gives n*n*(n+1)*(n-1)!D_{n-1}; quotient by column and colour permutations identifies relative derangement up to conjugacy/inversion, hence cycle type. An injection first row has (n+1)! possibilities, while second row has D_{n+1}+D_n possibilities, establishing fraction and Stirling/derangement asymptotic. For n=2 a 1-point derangement is absent; four-colour C4 solution has 24 assignments. Independent direct proper-coloring adjacency enumeration agrees at n=3..7 (72,960,32400,1330560,74793600).
